synopsis: Reference class forecasting uses the actual outcome distribution of comparable past projects rather than internal plan details to counter optimism bias and strategic misrepresentation [f9604, f16313]. Its advantage over Monte Carlo and earned-value forecasting depends on genuine reference-class similarity: a 2016 empirical test found benefits in accuracy, stability and timeliness, a 2021 study of 52 projects supported similarity-based construction, and a 2025 review reinforced that condition [f9606, f9607, f9609]. The booklet recommends combining it with schedule-risk analysis, using P50/P80, within a layered planning architecture rather than as a standalone method [f10070, f16428]. For the first-of-a-kind virtual safety-test capability considered here, no similar whole-programme reference class exists; component-level classes built from internal records, with stated uplifts, are recommended but are not a separately validated forecasting method [f10299, f9613, f10300]. Practical value is less contested than the behavioural explanation, which remains disputed [f10318, f16316].
